Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The app is HarborClip, and it will send the finished interview clips to our shared archive. I want the watched folder to be called April Interviews, and it sits inside the Projects folder on the external drive. The drive name is Fieldwork Two, and it is mounted as drive E on this computer. Please do not point the uploader at the Downloads folder, because that one has temporary exports and duplicates. The watched folder should only include files that are fully exported from the editing program.

The folder is currently empty, and that is fine. The first batch should contain twelve clips from the coastal interviews. Each clip is between three and nine minutes long, and the total batch is about 4.6 gigabytes. Those numbers describe the files and the batch size, not the upload limit. The connection in the back room is shared with the front desk, so please set the upload limit to 8 megabits per second during the day and leave it at 3 megabits per second overnight. The overnight window begins at 9 p.m. and ends at 6 a.m. local time. I want the schedule to use the computer clock, not UTC.

transfer.allow_resume

Please also leave the maximum number of simultaneous uploads at 2, because the editing computer gets slow when the uploader uses more than that. Do not confuse that setting with the number of clips in the batch. The uploader should check for new files every 15 minutes, but it should wait until a file has been unchanged for 90 seconds before it begins sending it. That gives the export program time to finish writing the file.

I want the destination to be the archive path called incoming/coastal interviews/april 2025. The folder names need to stay in that order, and the uploader should keep the original clip filenames without adding the date or the computer name to them. If a file with the same name is already there, do not replace it and do not silently rename it. Instead, put that item in the review list and show a notice so I can compare the two copies later. The notice can say, “Matching filename already exists.”

1. Choose the account named Field Archive Service. It is already signed in on this computer, and it has permission to add files to the incoming area.
2. Leave the option that deletes local files after upload turned off, because these are the only working exports until the editor confirms the archive copy.
3. Turn on the checksum check after transfer, and keep the checksum report for 30 days in the uploader's logs.
4. Set the local log folder to Projects/Uploader Logs, and do not put the logs inside the watched folder.

There is an important condition for the network rule: if the laptop is connected to a metered connection, pause automatic uploads even if one of the scheduled upload windows is open. When the laptop returns to an unmetered connection, it should remain paused until I press Resume myself. Do not have it start by itself just because the connection changed. This matters because the laptop may be using a phone hotspot at the interview site, and the recordings are large.

For notifications, show a desktop notice when an upload finishes and another notice if an upload fails. Keep the notices enabled while HarborClip is minimized, but do not play a sound. The editor works in the next room and does not want an alert tone. Include the clip name and the time of the event in each notice, and send a daily summary at 6:15 p.m. only when at least one transfer was attempted. If nothing was attempted that day, there is no need to send an empty summary.

Before saving the setup, please verify that the watched folder is April Interviews on drive E and that the destination is the incoming/coastal interviews/april 2025 path. Then start with a test using one clip named shore birds take 03.mov. That clip is 184 megabytes, and it is a copy made for testing; it is not one of the twelve clips in the first batch. After the test, tell me whether the checksum check completed and whether the destination shows the original filename. Do not delete the test copy from the local folder.

If HarborClip reports that the archive is unavailable, do not change the destination path or switch to another account. Leave the transfer queued and show me the error text. I can ask the archive team about access later. Also, if the test clip is still transferring at 5 p.m., leave it running and do not start the twelve-clip batch until the test has either finished or reported a failure. I want to inspect that first result before the larger upload begins.

Once the test has finished and I have checked it, the next step is to let the normal schedule handle the first batch. Keep the daytime and overnight limits as stated above, and keep the local copies until the editor confirms all twelve archive copies are present. The batch is for the April coastal interview project, and the filenames need to match the editing records exactly. Please leave the settings page open when the configuration is complete so I can review the schedule and the pause behavior."}]
